Failure to comply with this notification obligation by the Data Controller constitutes an offence and is liable to a fine of up to RM250,000.00 or imprisonment for a term of up to two years, or both;
(c) the obligation of Data Processors to adhere to Security Principle and take steps to protect personal data from loss, misuse, unauthorized access and other risks;
(d)provisions relating to the right of the data subject to request Data Controller to transmit their personal data to another data controller of their choice, subject to technical feasibility and compatibility of the data format;
(e)the introduction of an additional mode of service of the service of a notice or any other document by way of electronic means;
(f)the recognition of biometric data (defined as personal data from technical processing of physical, physiological or behavioral traits) as a type of sensitive personal data requiring stricter consent and security requirements; and
(g)Data Controllers may now transfer any personal data to any place outside Malaysia provided that the recipient jurisdiction’s laws are substantially similar to, and offer an adequate level of protection which is at least equivalent to the PDPA 2010.

Corporate Income Tax
Corporate income tax (“CIT”) in Vietnam is governed by the Law on Corporate Income Tax and the corresponding guiding documents from time to time. According to the Law on Corporate Income Tax, which was promulgated on June 3, 2008, came into effect on January 1, 2009, and amended by the Law on amendments to the Law on Corporate Income Tax 2013, the Law on amendments to the laws on taxation 2014 and the Law on Investment 2020 (“Law on CIT 2008”), and the Law on Corporate Income Tax, which was promulgated on June 14, 2025, came into effect on October 01, 2025 (“Law on CIT 2025”), replacing the Law on CIT 2008, a standard income tax rate of 20% shall be applied to enterprises that have established under the laws of Vietnam, foreign enterprises with or without permanent establishment. Law on CIT 2025 adds tax rates of 15% and 17%, applicable respectively to enterprises with total annual revenue not exceeding VND 3 billion and those with total annual revenue exceeding VND 3 billion but not exceeding VND 50 billion.
In principle, under Law on CIT 2008 and Law on CIT 2025, the difference between Total Revenue — Deductible Expenses is considered an income from main business activities, which is entitled to CIT incentives, if any. Normally, under Law on CIT 2008, Law on CIT 2025 and its corresponding guiding documents, other forms of income such as gains from foreign exchange revaluation, income from disposal of fixed assets, interest income, etc. not related to the main business are not entitled to CIT incentives, and thus shall be subject to the standard CIT rate of 20%. On the other hand, under Law on CIT 2008, an expense might be deductible for CIT purpose if the following conditions are met: (i) such expense is actually incurred and relevant to the company’s business activities, (ii) such expense must be supported by proper documents, (iii) payments above VND20 million must be supported by bank payment vouchers (or deemed as made via banks), (iv) such expense is not in the list of non- deductible expenses. However, with respect to deductible expenses, the Law on CIT 2025 retains conditions (ii), and (iv) as provided under the Law on CIT 2008, while condition (i) will be supplemented to include expenses in relation to the enterprise’s research and development activities calculated as a percentage of the actual expenses incurred during the tax period and condition (iii) will be amended to require that expenses must be supported by non-cash payment documents in cases of purchases of goods or services and other payments with a value of VND 5 million or more per transaction. Non-cash payment documents must comply with the relevant regulations under the laws on value-added tax. In addition, the Law on CIT 2025 introduces provisions allowing enterprises to include certain other actual expenses in deductible expenses when determining taxable income, provided that such expenses satisfy conditions (ii) and (iii) as mentioned above under the Law on CIT 2025. These expenses may include those incurred for the enterprise’s production and business activities that have not yet corresponded to the revenue generated in the period, in accordance with Government regulations; scientific research, technological development and innovation, and digital transformation; the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions for the purposes of carbon neutrality and net zero, mitigation of environmental pollution, and which are connected with the enterprise’s production and business activities, etc.
Under the Law on CIT 2008 and the Law on CIT 2025, regarding tax losses, tax losses are carried forward within a maximum period of 5 years after the loss- making year. Carry-back of tax loss is not allowed. Under the Law on CIT 2008 and its guiding documents, losses from incentive business activities can be offset against income from non-incentive activities, and losses from the transfer of real estate, investment projects, rights to participate in investment projects (except for mineral exploitation and exploration projects) can be offset against profits from other business activities. Under the Law on CIT 2025 and Decree No. 320/2025/ND-CP, which was issued by the Government on December 15, 2025 and came into effect on the same date, losses from business activities can be offset against income from other business activities, except for income from the transfer of real estate, investment projects and rights to participate in investment projects, which cannot be offset against income from incentive business activities.
Regarding capital assignment profit tax, although not specifically a separate tax, under the provisions of Law on CIT 2008, Law on CIT 2025 and its corresponding guiding documents, Capital Assignments Profit Tax (“CAPT”) applies a 20% tax to gains from assignment of capital in limited liability companies in Vietnam. The time of determining income from the transfer of capital shall be the time at which ownership of such capital is transferred.

Dividend distribution
Under the Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements to which Vietnam is a party, Vietnam is entitled to levy taxes on dividend income. Under the provisions of Law on CIT 2008, Law on CIT 2025 and its corresponding guiding documents, Vietnam has not yet imposed tax on income from dividends of enterprises, thus, there is no CIT on dividends paid to corporate shareholders. Nonetheless, a 5% personal income tax shall be applied on dividends paid to individual shareholders, whether the individual is tax resident or non-resident.
